statement: On stream, Decu's 9 entries of >=1 SOL were into tokens 1-25 s old (one at ~4 min); in 8 of them the creator had already sold more SOL than they put in before Decu bought, 7 within 2-30 s of the creator's first sell; those creators had put in 3.0-5.5 SOL. Across all 2,832 tokens launched in the window only 8.4% had a creator buy of >=2.9 SOL already sold at a profit by age 25 s. The exception (BLACK) was bought in its first second and sold 1 s later.

Decu's main entry is buying the first seconds after a new token's creator takes profit, on tokens they have pre-screened by narrative (linked X post) and by who is involved (labelled deployer and trader wallets in the tracker), then exiting within ~1 minute.
notes: claude:decu-stream-2026-10-01; alternatives: the trigger is the tracker feed (other labelled wallets buying) or Pulse momentum, and the creator's sell is incidental because nearly every new token's creator sells in its first seconds — test against a base rate before relying on this

statement: Among 328 creator-dump candidates during the stream, Decu bought 8. At the trigger their picks had about twice the live activity of the skips (unique buyers in 10 s 20 vs 8, creation-block buyers 7 vs 3) and more, not fewer, sniper holdings. A simulated bot entering every candidate lost -0.134 SOL per 1-SOL trade; on Decu's picks it made +0.267 (wins 67% vs 14%, p=0.0052). Activity filters alone stay negative (best -0.084).
notes: claude:decu-choice-2026-10-01; exploratory and in-sample, few picks; Decu's selection uses something the tape features here do not capture (X link is on ~all candidates, so it does not separate them)

statement: Tracked wallets pick the hottest brand-new tokens of the moment: median pick is 22 s old and in the ~96th-97th percentile of its ~190-token choice set for unique buyers (10 s) and inflow (30 s), entering after a ~14% dip from the 60-s high.
notes: claude:selection-2026-10-01; n_supporting approximates entries above the 90th percentile on buyers

statement: The visible profit of these traders comes at or before their own entry (timing/selection plus the follower flow their buy triggers), so copying their on-chain buys is not a viable strategy; any edge must come from anticipating the entry, not reacting to it.
notes: claude:copy-finding-2026-10-01; copy simulations (reports/simulations/overnight_train.md) agree on 9 wallets

statement: Waiting out the first frenzy and avoiding sniper-heavy supply, then exiting quickly on weakness, is the human-paced behaviour most associated with profit; chasing the hottest seconds is associated with loss.

Profitable human-paced wallets (380) enter later (~1 min old vs ~30 s), into less frenzied activity (10 vs 16 buyers/10 s; 2.8 vs 5.7 SOL inflow/30 s) with less sniper overhang (2.2% vs 4.8%), average down less (10% vs 24% of trips) and take smaller losses (-16.5% vs -29.7%) than losing ones (592).
notes: claude:human-winners-2026-10-01; n = winners of winners+losers; associations, not causes

statement: A copier entering 0.5-2 s after a tracked buy captures none of that move: median mid-price return over the next 3-10 s is about 0% to -2% before ~2.5% round-trip fees.
notes: claude:copy-finding-2026-10-01; n_supporting = grid cells with positive median (9 cells)

statement: Right after a kolscan-tracked wallet buys on the bonding curve, other wallets' net buying jumps (~0.1 -> ~0.5 SOL/s in the next 5 s) and the price is up a median ~18% at +5 s vs the pre-entry price, fading to below the pre-entry price by +180 s; random same-moment tokens show neither.
notes: claude:copy-finding-2026-10-01; up at +5s counted as supporting

statement: On the pump.fun bonding curve, realized profit concentrates in creation-block entries (mostly token creators buying their own launch and selling within seconds) and sub-5-second flippers; human-paced wallets are net negative in aggregate (-58.98 SOL), with 384 of 1317 profitable.
notes: claude:market-structure-2026-10-01; n_supporting = unprofitable human-paced wallets; one hour of data so far, re-run on full train

statement: Part of what separates their BUY from SKIP among equally hot tokens is supply structure: they avoid tokens whose developer and early snipers still hold supply that can be dumped ('dev sold and the market absorbed it' as an entry condition).
notes: claude:selection-2026-10-01; tape-only proxy for Axiom's dev/sniper fields; narrative/social inputs not yet observed

statement: Among tokens matching that profile, the ones no tracked wallet buys next fall a median -18% at 30 s and -32% at 60 s; the ones they do buy are ~flat/up (+4% at 60 s). Bought ones typically have the developer already sold out and fewer sniper wallets still holding (median ~7.7% vs ~14.3% of supply).
notes: claude:selection-2026-10-01; part of the bought-group lift is the follower flow their own buy causes
